'''Mandarb''' is the name of the [[horse|black stallion]] ridden by [[al'Lan Mandragoran]]. 

==History==
His name means "[[Blade]]" in the [[Old Tongue]].{{Ref/book|1|13}} Mandarb is a highly trained warhorse and, like his master, is a living weapon.  He is fiercely loyal to his master, allowing no one near himself without Lan's approval. So far, other than Lan, only Nynaeve has been able to approach and touch Mandarb with impunity.{{Ref/book|11|20}} Mandarb remains in the general location of Lan at all times.

==Activities==
A notable accomplishment of Mandarb is when he threw himself into a ruined [[Waygate]], forcibly opening it to let [[Moiraine Damodred]], Lan, [[Loial]] and the young adults of the [[Two Rivers]] to escape the [[Ways]] while [[Machin Shin]] pursues them.{{Ref/book|1|45}}

Mandarb is also notable for having, after a brutal attack from the [[Dreadlord]]s led by [[Mazrim Taim]] in a precursor to [[The Last Battle]], returned to the [[Borderlander]] camp against all odds. He sustained an injury on his left flank which leaves him permanently scarred, yet his reputation as a fierce warhorse and weapon is intensified as a result. 

At one stage, [[Zarine Bashere]] called herself Mandarb, but changed this to [[Faile]] after [[Perrin]] laughs and tells her it is the name of Lan's horse.

==Background==
Mandarb is one of two horses mentioned in ''[[The Eye of the World]]{{Ref/book|1|13}}'' that appear in ''[[A Memory of Light]]''{{Ref/book|14|e}}, [[Bela]] being the other{{ref/book|14|37}}.
